items.author: Claude (found by the BL-1033 lane on 2026-09-17, flagged by its cold review; filed by the main session)
items.title: A copied world does not tick byte for byte as its original: find the unfaithful copy and make world copies exact
items.design:
SCHEDULED (Ben, 2026-09-18, NR-890): early in sprint 45, ahead of Beat 1 — Beat 1 and the wizard's time-lapse round are the likeliest first features to copy a world and tick it.

FOUND 2026-09-17 by the BL-1033 lane (charter budget cost), probing whether one pre-landscape world per seed could be copied per matrix row. On seed 28 a copied base world matched the BL-1031 pins at D_search and D_land, but after the 12-tick validation settle it digested D_settle 18F78EB9B2B20F29 against the pinned 265C48A23E313B1A — whether copied before the landscape or after it — while the original world, settled with a copied recipe_registry, matches the pin. So `world`'s copy is faithful as data and unfaithful as a program: something the tick path reads differs between an original and its copy. Suspected (not located): an unordered container whose iteration order depends on insertion/rehash history, a pointer-keyed cache, or a cache the copy constructor carries stale.

WHY IT MATTERS. The simulation is deterministic by standing rule. The landscape search copies the base world for every evaluation (landscape_search.cpp score_one) but only scores statically, so today's shipped worlds are unaffected; any future feature or instrument that copies a world and then ticks it (a what-if preview, a save-branch, a matrix instrument) silently diverges. The harness comment in tools/verify/harness_params.hpp above build_app_base_world is the only other record.

THE WORK. A minimal reproduction in a harness (build seed 28 in app order, copy, settle both, compare snapshot bytes per tick to find the first tick that diverges), then bisect the tick path to the reading that differs, then fix the copy (or the container) so a copy ticks byte for byte. DONE WHEN: the reproduction passes on the 16 library seeds with the BL-1031 pins unmoved; if the fix must change iteration order on the ORIGINAL path, that is a world-mover and needs Ben's re-bless authorisation first.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-18, NR-886 item 4: read each over a window long enough to answer it); Claude (item text)
items.title: Three harness rows that went red on the 12-tick settle read over a window long enough to answer their own question
items.design:
WHY. BL-1008 moved these harnesses onto the app's 12-tick validation run, and three rows went honestly red because 12 ticks cannot answer them: spawn_solvency R4 (no rival fields a standing force within 12 ticks), acquisition_viability R1 (judges one quarter), and material_floor's "dead" definition (zero output across the whole settle). RULED (Ben, 2026-09-18, NR-886): read each over a window long enough to answer it — never reword a row to pass, and never shorten what it asks.

THE WORK. For each row, state the question it asks, the window that can answer it (in ticks, with the reason), and run the row over that window AFTER the validation run, using tools/verify/harness_params.hpp's run_app_validation_settle followed by run_app_live_window (BL-1033), so the world is the app's. Keep the 12-tick settle as the start state; do not change it. A row that is still red over its honest window stays red, recorded with its reading.

DONE WHEN. Each of the three rows prints the window it reads and its verdict over that window, on the 16 library seeds or a stated subset; the harness runtime is recorded; the BL-1031 pins are untouched (no src change).

items.author: Ben (2026-09-18, sprint 45 elicitation); Claude (item text, from a five-lane engine read with an adversarial check per lane)
items.title: A span resumed from a handoff struct carries its dated objects, keeps its 1200 anchors explicitly, and proves it under a fidelity check
items.design:
WHY (engine read, 2026-09-18, checked). run_history_sim resumes only four tables (resume_polities/grudges/contacts/corridors, history_sim.hpp:1713-1721; copy at history_sim.cpp:1490-1496). exploration_output already holds dated_objects and trade_flows, but a span open drops them, so: every treaty clause and tribute is lost; round 1 re-forms treaties against an EMPTY flow table, which INFLATES pair_trade_value_q (it subtracts only other partners' flows, cpp:1263-1301) and can bind far pairs the history never bound; the re-formed treaties all expire together 80 years later. Consolidation fires on year == params.start_year (cpp:902) and the near-home cutoff reads first.year < params.start_year (cpp:870, :3458, :3519; trace-only :3431, :4446), so a 1660 open would re-sweep every seat's stores into the capital (a second windfall, feeding Beat 1's capital paid in) and reclassify the 1,250 pairs met after 1200 as near-home. out.civilisations and out.universal_creeds start empty on a resume while the region/polity indices into them carry (settlement.hpp:473, :613; history_sim.hpp:2345), so a new record reuses index 0 and a known pair is recorded twice (cpp:3876-3916). A resumed span notes EVERY polity, dead ones included, as founded at its open (cpp:2598-2599).

RULED (DIGITISATION.md, the span paragraphs; PROPOSED 2026-09-18 and not overturned): the span is its own call resumed from exploration_output; consolidation and near-home stay anchored at 1200; trade flows need no pointer of their own, because the round-1 upkeep rebuilds them from dated_objects before any read (cpp:787-791, :1157, :3327 precede :3462).

THE WORK. (1) A resume_dated_objects pointer, copied beside cpp:1493-1496; the Exploration caller leaves it null. (2) consolidation_year and near_home_cutoff_year as explicit history_sim_params, read at every site above; Exploration sets both to empires_stop_year, which is its own start_year, so it is byte-identical. (3) Carry the civilisation and universal-creed tables across a resume (or re-key their indices) — check the digests before calling it non-moving. (4) A resumed span notes only living polities as founded (event layer, record_playback only). (5) A resume-fidelity check in digitisation_sim_harness: resume from the fixture's exploration_handoff at 1660 (rebuild creed_state from cultures; works and terrain from the fixture); GATE that the opening state equals the struct field for field and that after one round treaties, the overlord graph and stocks equal the continued run's 1660 round apart from the named network sources; REPORT the 1960 divergence against --through attributed by source (the 1660 corridor record, the dead-filter, the seed). Never gate it bit for bit — a lossless resume cannot equal the continued run, because a span reads its inherited corridor record until it closes (cpp:3327, :3420, :7312-7352) and the handoff filters corridors over the span's dead (cpp:8483-8493).

DONE WHEN. world_determinism digests unchanged; player_seed_sweep --digest-check holds (16 seeds, or a stated subset while BL-1034 runs); exploration_sim_harness green; history_sim_harness at its tracked 2-failure baseline (R3a2/R3a3); the fidelity check passes on the 16 library seeds and prints its divergence table.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-18, sprint 45 elicitation); Claude (item text, from a five-lane engine read with an adversarial check per lane)
items.title: A resumed span reopens a bought road rung at the tier it was bought to, behind a switch the sprint 45 re-bless turns on
items.design:
RULED (Ben, 2026-09-18, sprint 45 elicitation): the fix rides sprint 45's one re-bless. This reopens the defect BL-959 (empire corridor upgrade records its uses) closed as a KNOWN UNDER-READ comment on 2026-09-16 (history_sim.cpp:2010-2015).

WHY. A resumed span seeds live road counts from the corridor record's `uses` (cpp:1832-1840), never from its `tier`. A bought rung sets the live count to the tier threshold but records one walk (Empires: cpp:2031 and :2040, supply_upgrade_material_cost 2000 at era_minus_one.cpp:137; a post road: :2066 and :2073), so it reopens at the tier its walks earn — already at 1200 for Empire-bought Tracks and Roads, and at 1660 for post roads. The error runs both ways: a refused walk held one short live but counted in the record resumes promoted (cpp:1979-1989). A post road reopened at tier 2 can be bought a second time (cpp:3388, :2059). Beat 1's rail sink is the rung above the post road, so a demoted post road would misprice it.

THE WORK. Seed each resumed corridor's live count from max(uses, threshold(tier)) and resolve the refused-walk promotion the same way, behind history_sim_params::resume_seeds_corridor_tier (default false). BL-1044 turns it on. Update the KNOWN UNDER-READ comment to say what now holds.

DONE WHEN. Switch off: world_determinism and --digest-check unmoved. Switch on, per library seed: corridors whose resumed tier changed, by span (1200 and 1660), and no corridor reopening below the tier it was bought to; no rung bought twice.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-18, sprint 45 elicitation); Claude (item text, from a five-lane engine read with an adversarial check per lane)
items.title: The Industry tree is invested in the sim behind a switch: every living polity enters at 1660, fuel reads a held seam, urban mass drives its rate
items.design:
RULED (Ben, 2026-09-18, sprint 45 elicitation): every living polity enters the Industry tree at its root at 1660 (TREES.md § Milestones); the root IN-SP-1a is ungated and Furnace Practice links to it, so both sides of the Fuel Doctrine are reachable (store and doc amended in the sprint 45 cut; tree_lint industry OK). PROPOSED, not overturned: `fuel` passes on ANY held region over the bar, not the held mean (INDUSTRY_TREE.md § Aims); the Industry research RATE reads the urban mass of the polity's largest held regions, superlinearly, never the scorer (TREES.md § State).

THE WORK, modelled on BL-930 (85501a31: +426 lines over 6 files). Generate src/world/industry_tree_data.hpp (node tools/session/gen_empire_tree_table.js industry: 45 nodes, 86 effect rows, 22 scorer terms). Add the polity triple (industry_mask, investing, progress), industry_available / choose_industry_node / rim, a third fold line beside cpp:7576-7577, and an invest block inside case sim_verb::invest (cpp:6102), all behind history_sim_params::industry_tree_enabled (default false) plus an industry_open_year param the span sets to 1660. Copy the EMPIRE scorer's gate_open (cpp:7745-7756), never the Exploration one that opens fuel and ore unconditionally (cpp:7917-7918), and read fuel as any held region >= the bar for this tree only; the empire and exploration term_value arrays are never touched. Index term_value by the generated scorer_term order and guard it (a store edit silently reorders the positional array). Make the fork-deciding terms real — threatened, labour_bound, furnace_lit, credit_bound, known (the contacts table exists, history_sim.hpp:3093; the comment at cpp:6234-6242 saying BL-908 has not landed is stale, fix it) — and pin ground_forest and tariff_pressure at 0, said on the face of the harness. Research rate: urban_population of the top-k held regions, summed and CLAMPED before an integer isqrt-based superlinear transform (no isqrt helper exists in src/world), replacing the industry slice for this tree only. Industry modifiers sum into the shared tree_mod_q, which feeds defence, cohesion and the other trees' research rates — intended inside the span, and the reason the switch must stay off on every shipped path until BL-1044.

LINT. Add the check BL-930's commit asked for: each fork side stays reachable while its partner is refused, under the sim's rules (excludes, ring open, OR travel, milestone requires/requires_fork); it must pass on all invested trees.

HARNESS. An Industry block in exploration_sim_harness in the T7.1/T7.2 shape: every keyed effect read (the key switch in tree_effect_reader_of has no default, so T7.1 is the real guard), availability, both fork sides reachable, rim, pinned stubs, and industry_mask == 0 at 1660 on a shipped world. IN-SP-3m's 'campaign tree' open is classified tree_gate and has no consumer — say so rather than pass it vacuously.

DONE WHEN. Switch off: world_determinism and --digest-check unmoved. Switch on over 1660 -> 1960 in a harness (the continued call is acceptable until BL-1040 exists): per seed, Industry nodes held (distribution), fork sides taken, rim holders, and the share of polities that never pass the fuel gate. tree_lint all OK with the new rule.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-18, sprint 45 elicitation); Claude (item text, from a five-lane engine read with an adversarial check per lane)
items.title: The charter spend takes a square-root cap under a density ceiling and opens a specialist on its centre's unspent points, and the cost table gains the rows to set them
items.design:
RULED (Ben, 2026-09-18, sprint 45 elicitation; DIGITISATION.md § 1, CORPORATION_GENERATION.md Pass 4 and Pass 6): the per-resource cap scales by a SQUARE ROOT of the body's charter capital under a named DENSITY CEILING below the 200-per-body guard, with its own unspent reason; a budget specialist's starting capital is its centre's UNSPENT points at a stated rate, in place of the 400 +/-40% draw. PROPOSED: the rate makes one specialist's price in points worth 400 credits.

THE WORK. (1) The budget path reads its OWN restated constants, k_charter_max_firms_per_body = 200 and k_charter_per_resource_firm_cap = 8 (corporation_generation.cpp:2576-2578), whose comment couples them to Pass 6's (:2168-2170). Replace their use (cpp:3091, :3119-3122, :3127-3132) with a rule in charter_spend_params: per-good cap = max(8, floor(8 * sqrt(B / B_ref))), where B_ref is the budget the legacy cap would spend and G (goods with demand on the body) is DEFINED EXPLICITLY and fixed before the walk — upkeep and construction demand are re-measured per firm (cpp:3106-3114), so an undefined G drifts as firms land. Break the Pass 6 coupling; leave cpp:2168-2170 alone. Keep the legacy bool modes selectable so every pinned digest holds. (2) A density ceiling F_max < 200 with unspent reason density_ceiling (enum count at charter_budget.hpp:146, the name switch, the sweep's unspent_reasons). (3) A capital rule in charter_spend_params: specialist capital = centre remainder x rate; the remainder is what the centre could not spend after its specialist and firms; no shipped default (the contract at charter_budget.hpp:73-81 stands: refuse <= 0). capital_params is default-constructed at cpp:2945 today. (4) The report gains firms per good per body, G, seat balance and a solvent flag. (5) Fix the budget_system.hpp:20 comment ('~2%/qtr'; the rate is 1.5%, budget_system.cpp:312-315).

ROWS. Seeds 0, 28, 46 at 1x/2x/4x synthetic: the sqrt rule with ceilings near 120 and 160, per-good tallies on every row, so the table finally holds rows between 81 and 150 firms. About 1-1.5 h at BL-1033's row cost; keep-awake; never copy a world and then tick it (BL-1034). Ends in a NEEDS_REVIEW call for B_ref's definition and the ceiling.

NOT A WORLD-MOVER: nothing under src/ builds a budget (charter_budget.hpp:17-18). DONE WHEN: --digest-check none, empty, zero and refused hold; the synthetic legacy-mode digests hold; the new rows are in charter_cost_sweep.json with their note; the call is filed.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-18, sprint 45 elicitation); Claude (item text, from a five-lane engine read with an adversarial check per lane)
items.title: The Digitisation span runs as its own call from exploration_output, 1660 to 1960, wherever Exploration runs, behind a switch
items.design:
RULED (Ben, 2026-09-18, sprint 45 elicitation): the span runs wherever Exploration runs, whatever the epoch; the epoch flip (NR-869) waits for the phase and changes the calendar alone. The span is its own call resumed from exploration_output (the sprint 45 goal). PROPOSED, not overturned: it takes its own seed fold, and it prices trade on the 1660 corridor record, fixed for the span.

WHERE. A third call between the Exploration fold (hard_coded_world.cpp:1201-1230) and generate_population_centres (:1370), so centres materialise from 1960 demography and gen_settlement (:2364) is post-span. It must respect stop_after_exploration (world_gen_config.hpp:84) so the seed-library fingerprints and exploration_sweep stay unmoved and cheap; add stop_after_digitisation and the wizard's label 14 (hard_coded_world.hpp:388-403; startup_screens.cpp:328-330, :806-839).

PARAMS. Start from exploration_sim_params (struct defaults plus overrides, era_minus_one.cpp:372-403), NEVER the Empires derivation — copying the wrong base silently changes the verb set (supply upgrades, universal creeds, army upkeep). Own seed constant beside exploration_sim_seed (era_minus_one.cpp:407-411). 4-year band: 75 rounds, 1660..1956. industry_tree_enabled on inside this span (BL-1038). The run predicate is 'Exploration ran', never epoch_year; on the superseded arc (epoch >= 1700) Exploration is off and so is this span.

SWITCH. digitisation_span_enabled, default false; BL-1044 turns it on.

HARNESSES. digitisation_sim_harness --through must drive THIS span, not stretch Exploration (it sets exploration_stop_year = through_year today, :568-569) — otherwise the done-when readings are Exploration's. Keep the 1660 control. Keep the continued run available and label its output a 1200-network run. exploration_sweep keeps stopping at stop_after_exploration.

DONE WHEN. Switch off: world_determinism, --digest-check and seed_library.js --check unmoved. Switch on in the harness: 75 rounds per seed, the thirteen readings per seed, span cost per seed (median and max, Release, serial, quiet machine), and BL-1036's fidelity check green.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-18, sprint 45 elicitation); Claude (item text, from a five-lane engine read with an adversarial check per lane)
items.title: Beat 1: regions with centres accrue located industry points from 1660 to 1960, from scale, their own fuel, Industry capacity and treasury paid in
items.design:
RULED (Ben, 2026-09-18, sprint 45 elicitation; DIGITISATION.md § Beat 1): capital is paid in as a CONSEQUENCE — each round a fixed share of the capital treasury's surplus after the round's bills converts to industry points; no polity scores it, so it adds no § 11 verb. This cut carries NO sink (rail, mechanised force and works stay the design and come later, each with its own measurement). PROPOSED, not overturned: the stock sits on each region with centres (the sim has no centre entity: settlement.hpp:526-553); a region's own fuel sets its rate as a soft factor with a floor; ground the sim founded is re-surveyed at 1660; treasury points land on the capital's own region.

THE WORK. (1) An int64 industry_points field on region, credited to the region itself each round (order-independent), inside the Digitisation span only. Rate = urban scale x fuel factor (soft, with a floor) x (1000 + the Industry industrial modifier)/1000. (2) Treasury paid in: a fixed share of the capital treasury's surplus after the round's army and navy bills. (3) Re-survey fuel between spans, in hard_coded_world.cpp where world& exists, into a NEW region field (survey_endowment from tiles), so sim-founded regions — which inherit parent energy_q x 0.7 and are never surveyed (history_sim.cpp:5978-5981) — read their own ground; the existing energy_q, the treasury endowment and the tree gate means stay untouched. (4) A captured region keeps its points (located stock); no transfer rule is needed because points are read per region at the handoff. (5) No narrowing: range-check before any int32 cast at the handoff and reject, never clamp.

READINGS (digitisation_sim_harness). Reading 8: points spread across regions and polities, the share held on surveyed vs re-surveyed ground, the fuel factor's spread, and rho(points, urban heads) printed — if points only restate headcount the reading proves nothing (§ 1). Reading 9 (Migration): report it as FAILING where it fails (11 of 16 seeds flat or falling today), never n/a.

DONE WHEN. Span off: digests unmoved. Span on: readings 8 and 9 per library seed; the points' accrual cost per seed.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-18, sprint 45 elicitation); Claude (item text, from a five-lane engine read with an adversarial check per lane)
items.title: A region's industry points become its campaign centres' charter budgets, built in world/* and passed by the app and its harness mirror alike
items.design:
PROPOSED (listed 2026-09-18, not overturned; DIGITISATION.md Part III): a region's points reach its campaign centres by the carve's slots; a carved centre dropped when its body is built out takes its share unspent.

WHY. The budget is keyed by campaign population-centre entity (charter_budget.hpp:28-71). The carve binds centre to region and rank and throws it away: carved_centre carries only {region, scale} (population_generation.cpp:99-103; slots :148-153; key = urban_population/k at :186-187; the body-built-out break at :582-583). nearest_region mis-binds spilled centres; anchors carry province_anchor (components.hpp:1184), coverage foundings carry no flag (:823).

THE WORK. (1) carved_centre carries key and rank; found_centre records a NON-SERIALISED centre -> (region, rank) index on world, beside gen_settlement (world.hpp:269-282). (2) A builder in a new world/* function (not charter_budget.hpp, which holds the types only): split each region's points over its carved centres by slot key with largest-remainder apportionment (as harness_params.hpp:715-730); anchors and coverage foundings get nothing; a dropped carved centre's share is counted under its own unspent reason. (3) Switch on both sides: app::start_new_game_prelude sets sp.budget and sp.spend and moves app.cpp:1071 to the 7-argument apply with the same budget, spend and a report (the budget must outlive the search); tools/verify/harness_params.hpp mirrors it; review the two diffs against each other (player_seed_sweep.cpp:405-410). Prices live where the stockpile budget is built, as named constants BL-1044 sets — never as charter_budget.hpp defaults. (4) The search-less shipped entry points (verify_api.cpp:518, main.cpp:137, :237) state or mirror the budget. (5) The stale 'nothing shipped passes a budget' comments change in the same commit (landscape_search.hpp:150-152, charter_budget.hpp:17-18, harness_params.hpp:98-103, app.cpp:1058-1065). (6) player_seed_sweep --charter-budget stockpile. (7) Add the stockpile to world_determinism's region fold.

DONE WHEN. With the span off the stockpile is empty and the legacy branch runs first (landscape_search.cpp:235-239): --digest-check with stockpile == none == the BL-1031 pins, 16/16. With the span on in a harness, a non-empty budget reaches the search on at least three library seeds, with every point accounted for by spend or reason.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-18, sprint 45 elicitation); Claude (item text, from a five-lane engine read with an adversarial check per lane)
items.title: Charter prices, the capital rate and the no-specialist world, measured on real stockpiles
items.design:
RULED (Ben, 2026-09-18, sprint 45 elicitation): the specialist's price is anchored to the SEAT MENU — the median library world offers about as many seats as a world with no budget (legacy rosters: 6, 6 and 8 specialists on seeds 0, 28 and 46; NR-886: about 6.8 per seed on the app's world); the no-specialist world is decided on this sweep; a specialist opens on its centre's unspent points.

THE WORLD. The Digitisation span world: digitisation_span_enabled on at epoch 0 in the harness, NEVER epoch_year = 1960 (the superseded arc, Exploration off). Never copy a world and then tick it unless BL-1034 has landed.

MATRIX. Specialist price m in firm charters (at least 2, 4, 8), two or three firm-charter prices P_f, the capital rate at its PROPOSED anchor (one specialist's price = 400 credits), and the sqrt rule with BL-1039's ruled constants. 16 seeds at 11 rows is about 18 h, so trim rows to what answers the calls and state the trim.

REPORT per row and seed. Specialists and shortlist size against legacy; worlds with NO specialist; specialists opening with zero capital, and the capital distribution; unspent by reason including province_cap, density_ceiling and the dropped-centre reason; firms per good; the density-follows-cities reading; tick ratio with the phase split; seat balance and trailing-net sign. Keep-awake; scan each row's per-tick maximum for a sleep-length outlier.

DONE WHEN. The table is in charter_cost_sweep.json (or a sibling file) with its note, and NEEDS_REVIEW carries the calls: P_f, m, the capital rate, the no-specialist world, and whether the per-province cap (PROPOSED held at 2) gives way on concentrated budgets.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-18, sprint 45 elicitation); Claude (item text, from a five-lane engine read with an adversarial check per lane)
items.title: Beat 1 ships: the span and the charter budget on by default at epoch 0, prices pinned, one re-bless, one cold review
items.design:
RULED (Ben, 2026-09-18, sprint 45 elicitation): the span runs on by default at epoch 0 and the flip waits for the phase; the re-bless carries the span, the budget and BL-1037's road-tier fix, and no other shipped-world defect (BL-1045 and BL-1046 stay unscheduled). A new pin set is taken for the new shipped world; the BL-1031 pins stay as legacy rows and are never overwritten.

THE WORK. Turn on digitisation_span_enabled and resume_seeds_corridor_tier by default. Pin the charter prices, the capital rate and the sqrt constants from Ben's rulings on BL-1039 and BL-1043, where the stockpile budget is built. Implement the no-specialist ruling and restore or state the one-is_player invariant (world.hpp:262-265; today the player is null and spawn_seat returns early, corporation_generation.cpp:3244-3247, spawn_seat.cpp:118-119); print it on the seat line (app.cpp:958-962) and count it per seed. Write the rulings into DIGITISATION.md § 1 and CORPORATION_GENERATION.md.

THE RE-BLESS (as practised in 32e04a19): Ben authorises against the shape, on a quiet machine, Release, serial, keep-awake. Record old -> new world_determinism digests (A/A records, not pins). player_seed_sweep gains an arc/mode field: legacy rows keep the BL-1031 pins, and the new shipped world gets its own pinned digests. seed_library: regenerate, --check, --bless — expect fingerprints to move ONLY through BL-1037 (the span sits after stop_after_exploration). Run haulage_measure with --epoch 0 explicitly (its far default is 1960, the superseded arc, haulage_measure.cpp:178). history_sim_harness against its tracked 2-failure baseline; story_check's 2 US-016 failures are pre-existing.

THE DONE-WHEN READINGS at 1960 per library seed, on the shipped world: density follows cities (firm count per market against the catchment's urban population, and against its good count — the BL-1029 baseline is rho(firms, urban) 0.431 vs rho(firms, goods) 0.460 on its upper-median convention) and industrialisation (points unevenly held, with the fuel reading visible). A cold review (code-reviewer, no authoring context) over the sprint's integrated diff, with a fix round budgeted; the reviewer reports from the diff and names confirming runs rather than running sweeps.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-18, sprint 45 elicitation); Claude (item text, from a five-lane engine read with an adversarial check per lane)
items.title: Empire-rim holders buy Exploration nodes during the Empires span, against the rule that a tree opens when its phase opens
items.design:
FOUND 2026-09-18 by the sprint 45 engine read (Industry tree lane, checked). Exploration investing is gated only on polity_holds_empire_rim (history_sim.cpp:6285-6290) and nothing resets masks between spans, so a polity that reaches the Empire rim before 1200 invests in the Exploration tree inside the Empires span. TREES.md § Milestones says a rim holder enters the next tree 'the moment that phase opens'. The code or the doc is wrong, and the fix is work.

NOT ON SPRINT 45's RE-BLESS (Ben, 2026-09-18, elicitation: offered as a rider, not taken). Fixing it moves every shipped world's Empires round, so it waits for a re-bless of its own or a later one it can ride. Gate Exploration investing on the phase (year >= empires_stop_year) as well as the rim, then measure what early investors lose.

items.title: A captured capital's treasury is stranded, where the design says a conqueror takes the stores standing in the seat
items.design:
FOUND 2026-09-18 by the sprint 45 engine read (industry-points lane, checked). When a capital falls the loser re-seats at held.front() and the treasury stays on the captured region (history_sim.cpp:3784-3806). The conqueror's upkeep reads only regions[q.capital].treasury, and consolidation fires once, at the span's start (cpp:886, :902-916), so a captured treasury is neither the loser's nor the winner's — it is stranded. EXPLORATION.md's located-stock rule says a conqueror who takes the seat takes the stores standing in it.

NOT ON SPRINT 45's RE-BLESS (Ben, 2026-09-18, elicitation: offered as a rider, not taken). Beat 1's industry points do not inherit the defect, because they are read per region at the handoff. Fix: fold a captured seat's treasury into the conqueror's capital at capture (or state that it stays and why), then measure; it moves shipped worlds.

items.title: The epoch flip: four >=1700 gates and the settlement stop year decouple, and the superseded arc is retired or named
items.design:
SCHEDULED FOR THE PHASE'S CLOSE (Ben, 2026-09-18, sprint 45 elicitation: the span runs on at epoch 0 and the flip waits for Beats 2 and 3; NR-869 makes the flip the phase's done-when). DIGITISATION.md: the flip changes the calendar alone.

WHY IT IS NOT ONE LINE (engine read 2026-09-18, checked). epoch_year feeds FOUR >= 1700 predicates and a stop year: the arc (era_minus_one.cpp:35, which turns Exploration off), the recipe band (era_band.hpp:42), the settlement pass's antiquity branch (settlement.cpp:1164 — founding schedule, Stage 4 furnace), antiquity_start (hard_coded_world.cpp:1595 — ruptures, the Charter Act, globalisation), and run_settlement's stop year (hard_coded_world.cpp:748). Decoupling only the arc regresses the Empires round's inputs. Consumers of an explicit epoch 1960 build the superseded arc today: world_determinism R4 (:654-676, asserts prehistory_years == 800), era_world_harness R5 (:112-118), haulage_measure's far mode (:178), main.cpp --epoch.

OWED FROM BEN: retire the superseded 1560 -> 1960 arc, or keep it behind one explicit legacy-arc field read by all four gates (never by the arc predicate alone) — which also needs a save_game decision (save_game.cpp:86-101 writes world_params).
